components.note: 真 (zhēn) is a sound clue for 镇 zhèn and 慎 shèn; 真 means real, true.

example.fact: 真 is the common 'really' in exclamations: 真好 'how nice'. As an adjective it means 'real': 真的 'true'. 真的吗？ is a standard 'Really?' and 真不错 is a modest compliment.

examples.pinyin: Tā zhēn piàoliang.
examples.english: She is really pretty.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhēn de bù xiǎng qù gōngyuán ma?
examples.english: Do you really not want to go to the park?

components.note: 著 (zhù / zhe) — older form of 着: 艹 plant + 者 (zhě) as sound. 着 is a variant with 羊 over 目; neither part gives the 'in progress' sense.
目 (eye) — the bottom. The eye family: 看, 眼, 睛, 睡. In 着 it is only part of a variant shape. Memory aid: 睡着 — eyes 目 shut, asleep.

example.fact: 着 after a verb gives a lasting state: 坐着 'sitting', 穿着 'wearing'. It is neutral on the action itself. Other readings include zháo ('to catch on', 睡着 'fall asleep') and zhuó in written words like 着手.

examples.pinyin: Tā zuòzhe kàn shū.
examples.english: He sits reading a book.

examples.pinyin: Dēng hái liàngzhe.
examples.english: The light is still on.

components.note: 彐 (hand-like part) — 事 is usually explained as a hand holding a tool or tally, 'handling business' — a hedged reading, not certain.
史 (history, scribe) — shares an ancient root with 事: a hand holding a recording tool. Both are about handling official 'matters'.

example.fact: 事 covers 'affair, matter': 有事 'be busy', 没事 'it's nothing / no problem', 出事 'have an accident'. It is a frequent word for abstract matters, while 东西 means physical 'things'.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǒudiǎn shìqing, xiān zǒu le.
examples.english: I have something to take care of, so I'm leaving first.

examples.pinyin: Méi shì, bié dānxīn.
examples.english: It's nothing, don't worry.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement and place, as in 道 way, 过 pass, 近 near; the radical hints at "here / this way". The 文 part is not a useful sound clue.
人 (person) — the top part. 个 is the general measure word, as in 一个, 这个, 那个.
丨 (a vertical tally) — under 人, read as one tally mark per person: counting individuals one by one.

example.fact: 个 itself, per its own etymology, depicts a tally mark stacked over 人 (person) — a picture of counting people one by one. 这个 simply attaches that default counter to the demonstrative 这 ("this") so it can stand alone as a pronoun, the same pattern behind 那个 ("that one") and 哪个 ("which one").

examples.pinyin: Zhège zhōumò nǐ yǒu kòng ma?
examples.english: Are you free this weekend?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ hěn xǐhuan zhège chéngshì.
examples.english: I really like this city.

meanings: variant of 怎麼|怎么[zen3 me5]

components.note: 心 (heart) — feelings and thought, as in 想 think, 思 ponder, 急 anxious; in 怎 it is only loosely linked to the question sense.
乍 (zhà) is a loose sound clue for zěn; 乍 also sounds out 作 zuò, 昨 zuó and 炸 zhà.
幺 (tiny, a thread) — 么 looks like 幺 and was borrowed as a simplified form for the light particle in 什么, 怎么, 这么. The shape does not explain the meaning today.
厶 (loop) — the visible lower part, a small curl. Memory aid: a tiny stroke 丿 over a curl — a 'little something' you ask about: 什么 what?

example.english: How do you pronounce this character?
example.fact: 怎么 alone asks "how" as an adverb before a verb (怎么念 "how do you read it"), while its close relative 怎么样 asks "how is X / how about X" as a stand-alone question about quality or status — a common point where beginners conflate the two.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ zěnme bù chī le?
examples.english: Why aren't you eating anymore?

examples.pinyin: Qù huǒchēzhàn zěnme zǒu?
examples.english: How do I get to the train station?

components.note: 王 (jade) — on the left, 王 is the jade radical, as in 球 ball, 玩 play, 理 reason; jade is bright and shows itself.
见 (jiàn, see) is a close sound clue (xiàn) and also fits the meaning: appear so it can be seen.
土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 地 earth, 坐 sit; 在 is "to be at a place".
才 (cái) is a close sound clue for zài; 才 also appears in 材 cái.

example.fact: 现 (built from 见, "to see", catching sight of something) plus 在 ("to be present, at") combine almost literally as "what is manifesting, present" — giving 现在 its meaning "now, at present" through a fairly transparent compositional image.

examples.pinyin: Xiànzài wǒ zài shàngbān.
examples.english: I'm at work right now.

examples.pinyin: Tā xiànzài zhù zài Guǎngzhōu.
examples.english: He lives in Guangzhou now.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — speech or assent: to say "OK". 可 is also a famous sound part: 河 hé, 歌 gē, 哥 gē, 何 hé all take their sound from it.
人 (person) — the right-hand part. The left part is a hook-and-dot, from an old tool-like shape. Meaning 'by means of, so as to' is not shown by the parts today.
Memory aid: a person 人 using a tool to get something done — 'by means of' (可以, 所以, 以前). A mnemonic, not proven etymology.

example.fact: Chinese splits English "can" three ways: 可以 for permission ("is it allowed"), 会 for a learned skill ("do you know how"), and 能 for physical or circumstantial ability ("are you able to right now") — a three-way distinction with no single English equivalent.

examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ kěyǐ tíngchē ma?
examples.english: Can one park here?

examples.pinyin: Nǐ bù kěyǐ zài zhèr chōuyān.
examples.english: You can't smoke here.

components.note: 灬 (fire) — heat and burning, as in 热 hot, 照 shine, 黑 black; a dot is a small spot like a spark.
占 (zhàn) is a loose sound clue for diǎn; 占 also sounds out 站 zhàn and 粘 zhān.

example.fact: 点 gives the hour: 三点 'three o'clock'. 一点 means 'a little' (说慢一点 'speak a bit slower'). It also means 'to order' dishes (点菜) and 'to tick, to nod' (点头).

examples.pinyin: Qǐng gěi wǒ yìdiǎn shuǐ.
examples.english: Please give me a little water.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen diǎn liǎng ge cài ba.
examples.english: Let's order two dishes.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — marks speech and spoken particles, as in 吗, 吧, 啊; 呢 is a question or emphasis particle.
尼 (ní) gives the sound: 呢 ne/ní, also in 泥 ní.

example.fact: 呢 makes a follow-up question that reuses the topic: 你呢？ 'And you?'. 我的书呢？ means 'Where's my book?'. It can also mark that something is going on: 他在睡觉呢. It is toneless.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ zài zuò shénme ne?
examples.english: What are you doing?

examples.pinyin: Tā hái zài shuìjiào ne.
examples.english: He's still sleeping.

components.note: 女 (woman) — women and family terms, as in 妈 mom, 好 good, 姐 sister; 女 (nǚ) also loosely echoes the rú sound.
口 (mouth) — speech; 如 originally meant "to follow, accord with", later "as, like"; also in 汝 rǔ and 茹 rú.
木 (tree) — trees and wood, as in 树 tree, 林 woods, 桌 table; the fruit hangs on the tree.
田 (field) here is the round fruit drawn on the tree. 果 also gives the sound for 课 kè and 颗 kē.

example.hanzi: 如果明天下雨,我们就不去了。
example.pinyin: Rúguǒ míngtiān xiàyǔ, wǒmen jiù bú qù le.
example.english: If it rains tomorrow, we won't go.
example.fact: 如 (from 女 "woman" + 口 "mouth" — a wife following her husband's spoken word, hence "as, like") and 果 (fruit hanging from 木 "tree", hence "result") combine almost literally into "as the result [would be]" — a vivid compositional image underlying the everyday word for "if".

examples.hanzi: 如果你累了,就休息一下。
examples.pinyin: Rúguǒ nǐ lèi le, jiù xiūxi yíxià.
examples.english: If you're tired, take a rest.

examples.hanzi: 如果我有钱,我就买大房子。
examples.pinyin: Rúguǒ wǒ yǒu qián, wǒ jiù mǎi dà fángzi.
examples.english: If I had money, I'd buy a big house.

components.note: 只 (only; measure word) — two old characters merged: 隻 zhī "a single (bird), measure word" and 只 zhǐ "only".

example.english: I can only speak a tiny bit.
example.fact: This 只 (zhǐ) is 'only'; the same-looking 隻 simplified to 只 is the measure word zhī for animals (一只猫). 只有 means 'only if' and 只要 means 'as long as'.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhǐ yǒu yí ge dìdi.
examples.english: I only have one younger brother.

examples.pinyin: Tā zhǐ hē shuǐ, bù hē kāfēi.
examples.english: He only drinks water, not coffee.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — cutting, as in 到, 分, 刻; to cut apart means separate.
另 (lìng, other) — separating things into "other" parts: 别 is another, different, or "don't".

example.english: Don't forget to bring an umbrella.
example.fact: 别 before a verb gives a command: 别走 'don't go'. It is a shortened form of 不要. The noun sense 'other' appears in 别人 'other people', and the sense 'to part' in 告别 'say goodbye'.

examples.pinyin: Bié shuōhuà, bǎobao zài shuìjiào.
examples.english: Don't talk, the baby is sleeping.

examples.pinyin: Biérén dōu zǒu le.
examples.english: Everyone else has left.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — marks speech, sounds and eating, as in 叫 call, 吃 eat, 唱 sing; 哦 is an interjection of understanding.
我 (wǒ) — loose sound hint only (ó vs wǒ).

example.fact: 哦 is read with different tones for different attitudes: ò (falling) means 'oh, I see', ó (rising) means 'oh?' with surprise or doubt, and ǒ shows puzzlement. The character stays the same; the tone carries the mood.

examples.pinyin: Ò, yuánlái shì zhèyàng a.
examples.english: Oh, so that's how it is.

examples.pinyin: Ò, wǒ wàngle dài yàoshi.
examples.english: Oh, I forgot to bring my keys.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 住 live.
旦 (dàn) gives the exact sound; 旦 also sounds out 担 dān and 胆 dǎn.

example.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng qù, dànshì méiyǒu shíjiān.
example.english: I want to go, but I don't have time.
example.fact: 但 on its own is fairly bookish; speech prefers 但是, 可是 or the softer 不过. It also appears in the pattern 不但…而且… 'not only…but also…'. Chinese does not pair it with 虽然 and an extra 'but' the way English sometimes does: 虽然…但是… uses both.

examples.pinyin: Tā hěn lèi, dànshì hái zài gōngzuò.
examples.english: He's tired, but he is still working.

examples.hanzi: 这件衣服很好看，但太贵了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu hěn hǎokàn, dàn tài guì le.
examples.english: This dress is pretty, but it's too expensive.

components.note: 衤 (clothing) — 衤 is the clothing radical, as in 衣, 裤, 衬; 被 is a quilt, then the passive marker.
皮 (pí) — loose hint — 被 is bèi; 皮 also sounds out 披 pī and 坡 pō.

example.pinyin: Wǒ de qiánbāo bèi tōu le.
example.fact: 被 builds the passive: object + 被 + (doer) + verb. Traditionally it signals something unfortunate (被骗 'be cheated', 被偷 'be stolen'), though modern usage has widened it. The doer can be left out, as in the example. The 'quilt' sense survives in 被子.

examples.pinyin: Dàngāo bèi dìdi chīwán le.
examples.english: The cake was eaten up by my younger brother.

examples.pinyin: Tā bèi lǎoshī pīpíng le.
examples.english: He was criticized by the teacher.

components.note: 走 (walk, run) — a person with swinging arms above a foot 止. As a radical it marks movement: 起, 越, 超, 趣.

example.fact: In modern Chinese 走 means 'walk' and 'leave' (我走了 'I'm off'), while 'run' is 跑. In classical Chinese it meant 'run', and that older sense survives in words like 奔走 and 走马 'galloping horse'.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zǒulù huí jiā ba.
examples.english: Let's walk home.

examples.pinyin: Tā gāng zǒu, nǐ méi kànjiàn ma?
examples.english: He just left, didn't you see?

components.note: 大 (big) — an extra stroke below emphasises it: bigger than big, too much. 太 also sounds out 泰 tài.

example.fact: 太 + adjective + 了 can complain or praise: 太贵了 'too pricey', 太好了 'great!'. But 不太 is the mild 'not very': 不太好 'not so good'. Keep 大 (dà) and 太 (tài) apart: the extra dot is what separates them.

examples.pinyin: Jīntiān tài rè le, bié chūqù.
examples.english: It's too hot today, don't go out.

examples.hanzi: 太好了，我们可以去玩了！
examples.pinyin: Tài hǎo le, wǒmen kěyǐ qù wán le!
examples.english: Great, we can go play now!

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement and place, as in 道 way, 过 pass, 近 near; the radical hints at "here / this way". The 文 part is not a useful sound clue.
木 (tree) — wood, as in 桌 table, 板 board; 样 once meant a tree (acorn) and later "form, pattern".
羊 (yáng, sheep) is a near-exact sound clue for yàng; 羊 also sounds out 洋 yáng and 养 yǎng.

example.fact: 这样 modifies *how* an action is carried out, usually right before a verb (这样做, "do it this way") — its near-synonym 这么 (also in this batch) more often modifies *degree* right before an adjective (这么好, "this good"), a distinction English's single word "this" doesn't make.

examples.pinyin: Zhèyàng zuò tài máfan le.
examples.english: Doing it this way is too much trouble.

examples.hanzi: 他总是这样,真让人生气。
examples.pinyin: Tā zǒngshì zhèyàng, zhēn ràng rén shēngqì.
examples.english: He's always like this; it's really annoying.

components.note: 田 (field) — farmland, the village's fields.
土 (earth) — land; field + earth gives "village" and then the unit of distance. 里 is the sound part of 理 lǐ.

example.english: The book is in the bag.
example.fact: 里 is the standard 'inside' word after nouns (家里, 包里) and is toneless there. In simplified writing 里 took over for the older 裡 'lining, inside', so one character now covers both 'inside' and the old unit of length (about 500 m).

examples.pinyin: Fángjiān lǐ yǒu yì zhāng dà chuáng.
examples.english: There is a big bed in the room.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de shǒujī zài bāo lǐmiàn ma?
examples.english: Is your phone in your bag?

components.note: ⻊ (foot, form of 足) — feet and walking: 跑, 路, 跳; 跟 first meant the heel, then to follow.
艮 (gèn) is a near sound match for gēn; same part in 根 gēn, 很 hěn, 恨 hèn.

example.english: I'm going together with a friend.
example.fact: 跟 is the casual, northern-style 'with/and', replacing 和 in speech: 我跟你说 'let me tell you'. 跟…一样 means 'the same as'. Its physical meaning 'heel' remains in 脚后跟 and 高跟鞋 'high-heeled shoes'.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ gēn nǐ yìqǐ qù mǎi cài.
examples.english: I'll go grocery shopping with you.

examples.hanzi: 请跟我来，我带你去办公室。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng gēn wǒ lái, wǒ dài nǐ qù bàngōngshì.
examples.english: Please follow me, I'll take you to the office.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — speaking, as in 说 say, 问 ask; 告 is "to tell". 告 also gives sound to 造 zào and 靠 kào.
讠 (speech, simplified 言) — words and language, as in 说 say, 请 please, 谢 thank.
斥 (chì) is only a loose sound hint for sù.

example.hanzi: 请告诉我你的电话号码。
example.pinyin: Qǐng gàosu wǒ nǐ de diànhuà hàomǎ.
example.english: Please tell me your phone number.
example.fact: 告诉 always names the listener directly after the verb (告诉 + person + thing, e.g. 告诉我 "tell me") — English "tell" can drop the listener, Chinese can't. Dictionaries also list a separate, fully-toned reading gàosù for a rarer legal sense, "to file a (private criminal) complaint" — the same two characters, a different register entirely.

examples.hanzi: 我告诉妈妈今晚不回家吃饭。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gàosu māma jīnwǎn bù huí jiā chīfàn.
examples.english: I told Mom I won't be home for dinner tonight.

examples.pinyin: Tā méi gàosu wǒ zhè jiàn shì.
examples.english: He didn't tell me about this.

components.note: 囗 (enclosure) — here a mat; oldest form shows a person 大 lying on a mat, "to rely on", later "cause". 因 also sounds out 姻 yīn and 烟 yān.
力 (strength) — visible inside 为. Memory aid: putting strength 力 into doing something; 为 is 'to do, to act' and, in 因为, 为什么, 'because/for'.
為 (traditional) — often explained as a hand leading an elephant to work. 为 is a cursive simplification, so the picture is no longer visible.

example.pinyin: Wǒ méi qù, yīnwèi wǒ shēngbìng le.
example.english: I didn't go, because I was sick.
example.fact: 因为 almost always shows up paired with 所以 (also in this batch, at rank 36) in the fixed construction "因为...,所以..." — where English would find "because...so..." together in one sentence redundant, Chinese speech very often keeps both halves.

examples.pinyin: Tā yīnwèi xiàyǔ méi lái shàngbān.
examples.english: He didn't come to work because of the rain.

examples.hanzi: 因为路上堵车,所以我迟到了。
examples.pinyin: Yīnwèi lùshang dǔchē, suǒyǐ wǒ chídào le.
examples.english: Because of traffic, I was late.

components.note: 自 (self) — picture of a nose; Chinese speakers point to the nose to mean "I", so it became "self" (compare 鼻 bí, nose, which adds 畀).
己 (oneself) — dictionary reads it as a loom with thread; scholars are not sure. Memory aid: a curled-up figure turned in on itself — 'self'. Sound clue in 记 纪 (jì) and 起 (qǐ).

example.hanzi: 她喜欢自己一个人旅行。
example.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan zìjǐ yí gè rén lǚxíng.
example.fact: 自 is a pictograph of a nose (people in ancient China pointed to their own nose to mean "me"), and 己 separately depicts a woven cord, also borrowed for "self" — 自己 doubles up two originally independent "self" pictographs into one intensified reflexive word.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ yào xiāngxìn zìjǐ.
examples.english: You have to believe in yourself.

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ zìjǐ zuò de dàngāo.
examples.english: This is a cake I made myself.

components.note: 冉 (rǎn) — the main part. The dictionary story is two fish on a line 一: a second catch, so 'again'. It is a memory aid; the origin is unclear.
一 (one) — the top bar. Memory aid: 'one more' line on top — 再见 see you again, 再次 once more.

example.english: Please say it one more time.
example.fact: 再 is for repeats that haven't happened yet: 再来一杯 'another cup'. For repeats that already occurred, use 又: 他又来了. 再见 'goodbye' literally means 'see (you) again'.

examples.pinyin: Míngtiān wǒ zài gěi nǐ dǎ diànhuà.
examples.english: I'll call you again tomorrow.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ zài chī yìdiǎnr ba.
examples.english: Have a little more.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — sound and speech, as in 吃, 唱, 问.
斤 (jīn, axe) is only a loose clue for tīng; the traditional 聽 had 耳 ear.

example.fact: 听 means 'listen', while 听见 or 听到 means 'actually hear'. 听说 introduces hearsay: 听说他走了 'I hear he left'. The simplified 听 reuses an old character that meant 'to smile', borrowed to replace the more complex 聽.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān wǎnshang tīng yīnyuè.
examples.english: I listen to music every night.

examples.pinyin: Duìbuqǐ, wǒ méi tīng qīngchu.
examples.english: Sorry, I didn't hear clearly.

meanings: variant of 這裡|这里[zhe4 li3]

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement and place, as in 道 way, 过 pass, 近 near; the radical hints at "here / this way". The 文 part is not a useful sound clue.
田 (field) — farmland, the village's fields.
土 (earth) — land; field + earth gives "village" and then the unit of distance. 里 is the sound part of 理 lǐ.

example.fact: 这里 (zhèlǐ) is the neutral, Mainland-standard word for "here"; Beijing-area speech commonly prefers the r-suffixed 这儿 (zhèr) instead, and Taiwan/Hong Kong writing uses 這裡 with the traditional 裡 — three regional flavors of the same word.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de shūbāo zài zhèlǐ.
examples.english: Your schoolbag is here.

examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ de fēngjǐng zhēn piàoliang.
examples.english: The scenery here is really beautiful.

components.note: 忄 (heart) — feelings, as in 怕, 忙, 情: a quick, glad heart.
夬 (guài) is a close sound clue for kuài; 夬 also in 块 kuài, 筷 kuài and 决 jué.

example.pinyin: Nǐ zǒu de tài kuài le.
example.fact: 快 + verb means 'about to': 快到了 'almost there'. It also forms 快乐 'happy' and 快点儿 'hurry up'. As an adjective it describes speed: 快车 'express train'. Its first sense of 'pleased' explains why it appears in 快乐.

examples.pinyin: Kuài diǎnr, wǒmen yào chídào le!
examples.english: Hurry up, we're going to be late!

examples.hanzi: 火车快到了，请你快一点。
examples.pinyin: Huǒchē kuài dào le, qǐng nǐ kuài yìdiǎn.
examples.english: The train is almost here, please be quick.

components.note: 讠 (speech; traditional 言) — marks speaking and questions, as in 说 say, 请 ask; 谁 is the question word who.
隹 (zhuī, short-tailed bird) — loose sound hint (shéi); 隹 also sounds out 堆 duī and 推 tuī.

example.fact: 谁 is spoken shéi, with shuí as the older or more formal reading. The question word stays in the sentence slot of the answer: 谁来了？ 'Who came?' For 'everyone', 谁 + 都 works: 谁都知道 'everyone knows'.

examples.pinyin: Shéi zài wàimiàn qiāo mén?
examples.english: Who is knocking outside?

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì shéi de yǔsǎn?
examples.english: Whose umbrella is this?

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 住 live.
旦 (dàn) gives the exact sound; 旦 also sounds out 担 dān and 胆 dǎn.
日 (sun) — on top; the usual explanation is sun over 正 "straight, correct": what is clear and straight is "right, is". A memory aid, not firm etymology.

example.hanzi: 这件衣服很贵,但是我很喜欢。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu hěn guì, dànshì wǒ hěn xǐhuan.
example.english: This piece of clothing is expensive, but I really like it.
example.fact: 但是 sits at the neutral, standard-register end of Chinese's "but" words — 可是 feels a shade more conversational, and 不过 is the softest and most casual of the three near-synonyms — useful to know when picking which "but" fits the tone of a sentence.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng qù, dànshì méiyǒu shíjiān.
examples.english: I'd like to go, but I don't have time.

examples.hanzi: 他很聪明,但是不太努力。
examples.pinyin: Tā hěn cōngming, dànshì bú tài nǔlì.
examples.english: He's smart, but not very hardworking.

components.note: 多 (many) — two 夕 stacked, repeated again and again: so "many, much, more".

example.english: There are a lot of people here.
example.fact: 多 before an adjective asks degree: 多大 'how old/big', 多远 'how far'. After a number it means 'and a bit more': 三十多个人. A noun usually needs 很 in front: 很多人, not 多人.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ jiā yǒu duōshao kǒu rén?
examples.english: How many people are in your family?

examples.pinyin: Jīntiān láile hěn duō kèrén.
examples.english: Many guests came today.

components.note: 用 (use) — early picture is debated: a pail, a fenced enclosure or a hung bell. Memory aid: a door-frame 冂 with a cross-bar — a tool 'put to use' (使用, 不用).

example.pinyin: Wǒ kěyǐ yòng nǐ de shǒujī ma?
example.fact: 用 'use' appears in 用中文说 'say it in Chinese'. Negated it means 'no need to': 不用谢 'no need to thank me', 不用了 'no, thanks'. It also forms 有用 'useful' and 没用 'useless'.

examples.pinyin: Zhège cí zěnme yòng?
examples.english: How do you use this word?

examples.pinyin: Nǐ búyòng zháojí, mànmàn lái.
examples.english: No need to rush, take your time.

components.note: 日 (sun) — day and time, as in 晴 clear, 早 early, 明 bright; time was read from the sun.
寸 (cùn) stands in for 寺 sì in the traditional 時; sound clue is loose. 寺 also gives 诗 shī and 持 chí.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 住; 候 means to wait for someone.
侯 (hóu) is a close sound clue for hòu; it also gives 猴 hóu monkey and 喉 hóu throat.

example.pinyin: Xiǎo de shíhou, wǒ zhù zài Shànghǎi.
example.english: When I was little, I lived in Shanghai.
example.fact: 时候 almost always appears inside the frame "...的时候" ("at the time when...") attached to a preceding clause, functioning like an English "when"-clause marker — for freestanding "time" as a concept or duration, Chinese instead reaches for 时间 (also in this batch, at rank 42).

examples.pinyin: Nǐ shénme shíhou huílái?
examples.english: When are you coming back?

examples.hanzi: 吃饭的时候不要看手机。
examples.pinyin: Chīfàn de shíhou bú yào kàn shǒujī.
examples.english: Don't look at your phone while eating.

components.note: 下 (below) — a mark placed under a line, the mirror of 上 above.

example.fact: 下 means 'next' in 下个月 'next month' and 下次 'next time'. Chinese says 下雨 for 'rain' (literally 'rain falls') and 下班 for 'finish work'. It is also a verb: 下车 'get off the vehicle'.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài lóuxià děng nǐ.
examples.english: I'll wait for you downstairs.

examples.pinyin: Xià cì wǒ qǐng nǐ chīfàn.
examples.english: Next time I'll treat you to a meal.

components.note: 己 (self) — 已 looks like 己 with the gap closed, so do not mix them up. Memory aid: the opening is closed — it is already done (已经).
纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads and cloth, as in 红 red, 给 give, 级 level; 经 first meant a warp thread, then "classics, pass through".
巠 (jīng), here simplified to look like 圣, gives the same sound; also in 茎 jīng, 径 jìng and 轻 qīng.

example.fact: 已经 is almost always paired with the sentence-final particle 了 to mark that something is complete ("已经...了"), much like English pairs "already" with a perfect-tense verb ("has already left") — a reliable pattern to reach for when building an "already" sentence.

examples.pinyin: Huǒchē yǐjīng kāizǒu le.
examples.english: The train has already left.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ yǐjīng chīguo fàn le ma?
examples.english: Have you eaten already?

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words, as in 说, 请, 诉: you thank someone with words.
射 (shè) is a loose sound clue for xiè; in 谢谢 the tone drops to neutral on the second.
讠 (speech) — words, as in 说, 请, 诉: you thank someone with words.
射 (shè) is a loose sound clue for xiè; in 谢谢 the tone drops to neutral on the second.

example.fact: 谢谢 is just 谢 ("to thank") reduplicated — doubling a single-syllable verb is a common Mandarin device that softens and formalizes it, the same pattern behind 看看 ("take a quick look") and 试试 ("give it a try").

examples.pinyin: Xièxie, bú yòng le.
examples.english: Thanks, no need.

examples.pinyin: Tā duì wǒ shuōle yì shēng xièxie.
examples.english: He said thank you to me.

components.note: 力 (strength) — visible inside 为. Memory aid: putting strength 力 into doing something; 为 is 'to do, to act' and, in 因为, 为什么, 'because/for'.
為 (traditional) — often explained as a hand leading an elephant to work. 为 is a cursive simplification, so the picture is no longer visible.
十 (shí, ten) is a loose sound clue for 什 (shén, shí in 什锦); old sense "a set of ten", hence "assorted". In 什么 it is simply "what".
幺 (tiny, a thread) — 么 looks like 幺 and was borrowed as a simplified form for the light particle in 什么, 怎么, 这么. The shape does not explain the meaning today.
厶 (loop) — the visible lower part, a small curl. Memory aid: a tiny stroke 丿 over a curl — a 'little something' you ask about: 什么 what?

example.fact: 为 ("for the sake of, because of") plus 什么 ("what") combine transparently into "for what [reason]" — unlike many Chinese question words, its literal logic maps almost directly onto the English phrase, making it one of the easier compounds to see through.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ wèishénme bù kāixīn?
examples.english: Why are you unhappy?

examples.pinyin: Tā wèishénme xué Zhōngwén?
examples.english: Why is he studying Chinese?

components.note: 见 (see) — seeing and perceiving, as in 现, 看, 视: 觉 is to sense and become aware (jué), also "sleep" (jiào) in 睡觉.
The top is a shape of 学 (xué), a loose sound hint from the traditional 覺.
彳 (step) — walking and going, as in 行, 往, 很 very.
寸 (hand) — oldest form is a hand grabbing a cowrie shell (money): 得 is "to obtain". The shell has worn down to 旦.

example.hanzi: 我觉得这个电影很有意思。
example.pinyin: Wǒ juéde zhège diànyǐng hěn yǒu yìsi.
example.english: I think this movie is very interesting.
example.fact: 觉得 introduces a subjective feeling or impression ("I feel/think that..."), while its more formal cousin 认为 is reserved for a reasoned belief or judgment — in everyday speech 觉得 dominates, while 认为 shows up far more in writing, debate, or argument.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ juéde yǒudiǎn lěng.
examples.english: I feel a bit cold.

examples.hanzi: 你觉得这件衣服怎么样?
examples.pinyin: Nǐ juéde zhè jiàn yīfu zěnmeyàng?
examples.english: What do you think of this piece of clothing?

components.note: 大 (big person) — a person with a line above the head, marking the sky above; tiān = heaven, sky, day.

example.pinyin: Wǒ měi tiān dōu xué Zhōngwén.
example.fact: 天 covers both 'sky' and 'day': 天空 sky, 三天 three days, 天气 weather. Doubled as 天天 it means 'every day'. It also reaches into abstract uses: 老天 'heaven', 天才 'genius'.

examples.pinyin: Jīntiān tiānqì zhēn búcuò.
examples.english: The weather is really nice today.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yì tiān yào hē sān bēi kāfēi.
examples.english: I drink three cups of coffee a day.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做; 像 is a person's likeness.
象 (xiàng, elephant) gives the exact sound; 象 first meant elephant, then "image".

example.pinyin: Nǐ zhǎng de hěn xiàng nǐ bàba.
example.english: You look a lot like your dad.
example.fact: 像 is 'to resemble', and 像…一样 'just like…' makes similes. 好像 means 'it seems'. 像 was formed by adding 亻 to 象, which originally also meant 'image', long before it meant 'elephant' in everyday use.

examples.pinyin: Zhège háizi xiàng tā māma.
examples.english: This child looks like his mother.

examples.hanzi: 今天的天气像春天一样。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān de tiānqì xiàng chūntiān yíyàng.
examples.english: Today's weather is just like spring.

meanings: variant of 這麼|这么[zhe4 me5]

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement and place, as in 道 way, 过 pass, 近 near; the radical hints at "here / this way". The 文 part is not a useful sound clue.
幺 (tiny, a thread) — 么 looks like 幺 and was borrowed as a simplified form for the light particle in 什么, 怎么, 这么. The shape does not explain the meaning today.
厶 (loop) — the visible lower part, a small curl. Memory aid: a tiny stroke 丿 over a curl — a 'little something' you ask about: 什么 what?

example.english: Why is the weather so hot?
example.fact: 么 is a recurring, toneless "helper syllable" that turns a root into a full colloquial word — the same 么 shows up in 什么 ("what"), 怎么 ("how"), and 那么 ("like that"), all also in this batch, forming a whole family of "-么" words built the same way.

examples.pinyin: Jīntiān de zuòyè zhème duō!
examples.english: There's so much homework today!

examples.pinyin: Wǒ méi xiǎngdào tā zhème gāo.
examples.english: I didn't expect him to be this tall.

components.note: 它 (it) — an old picture of a snake; 蛇 shé (snake) adds 虫. Its pronoun use is borrowed. Sound series: 拖 tuō, 驼 tuó.

example.pinyin: Tā shì yì zhī kě'ài de xiǎo gǒu.
example.english: It is a cute little dog.
example.fact: 它 refers to things and animals; people are 他 or 她. In Chinese the subject 'it' is often dropped (很好吃 'it's tasty'). Plural is 它们. In Taiwan 牠 was traditionally used for animals, though 它 is common today.

examples.pinyin: Tā zài yuànzi lǐ wán qiú.
examples.english: It is playing with a ball in the yard.

examples.hanzi: 这只猫很可爱，我很喜欢它。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhī māo hěn kě'ài, wǒ hěn xǐhuan tā.
examples.english: This cat is cute, I like it a lot.

components.note: 人 (person) — one person following another: 从 means to follow, then "from".

example.fact: 从 gives a starting point: 从这里到那里 'from here to there'. 从来 means 'ever' and 从来不 'never'. Its roots are the picture of one person following another, which is the older meaning 'to follow'.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ cóng bā diǎn kāishǐ gōngzuò.
examples.english: I start work at eight o'clock.

examples.pinyin: Cóng wǒ jiā dào xuéxiào hěn jìn.
examples.english: It's close from my home to school.

components.note: 儿 (legs, person) — with a foot 𠂉 above: a foot stepping out in front of a person, so "first, earlier".
土 (earth) — a green shoot pushing up from the ground: growth, birth, life. 生 also sounds out 性 xìng, 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.

example.pinyin: Wáng xiānsheng, hěn gāoxìng rènshi nǐ.
example.english: Mr. Wang, nice to meet you.
example.fact: 先生 literally means "one born before" (先 "before" + 生 "born") — originally an honorific for a teacher or elder, someone who came before you in age or learning. It broadened over time into today's generic "Mr./sir", while still surfacing as "teacher" in some contexts.

examples.pinyin: Lǐ xiānsheng shì wǒ de lǎoshī.
examples.english: Mr. Li is my teacher.

examples.hanzi: 请问,这位先生要点什么?
examples.pinyin: Qǐngwèn, zhè wèi xiānsheng yào diǎn shénme?
examples.english: Excuse me, what would this gentleman like to order?

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打 hit, 拿 take, 把 hold; 找 is to search with the hands. The right part 戈 is not a useful clue.

example.pinyin: Wǒ zài zhǎo wǒ de shǒujī.
example.fact: 找 is 'search for'; 找到 is 'found it', so they are different results. 找 can also mean 'to give change' (找您五块 'here's five yuan back') and 'to visit': 我来找你.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ zài zhǎo shénme dōngxi?
examples.english: What are you looking for?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhǎodào wǒ de yàoshi le.
examples.english: I found my keys.

components.note: 取 (qǔ, take) is the base; the loose sound clue also appears in 趣 qù and 娶 qǔ. The top 日 here is an old cap shape, not the sun.

example.fact: 最 forms superlatives before an adjective or verb: 最大 'biggest', 最近 'recently', 最后 'last'. No 很 is needed. Don't confuse 最 (zuì) with 取 (qǔ); the top part differs.

examples.pinyin: Tā shì wǒ zuì hǎo de péngyou.
examples.english: He is my best friend.

examples.hanzi: 这里最热闹的地方是哪儿？
examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ zuì rènao de dìfang shì nǎr?
examples.english: What's the liveliest place around here?

components.note: 壴 (zhù, drum) — a drum on top of 口 mouth: music and singing, joy.
口 (mouth) — singing and speaking, as in 唱 sing, 吃 eat.
欠 (yawn, open mouth) — breath and mouth actions, as in 歌 song, 吹 blow.
又 here replaces 雚 (huān) in the traditional 歡, so it is only a stand-in; same shorthand in 观 and 劝.

example.fact: 喜 already means "joy" on its own (built from 壴, a drum, plus 口, a mouth — a picture of singing and drumming in celebration), and 欢 separately means "happy, joyous" — 喜欢 doubles up two near-synonymous "joy" characters, a common Chinese strategy for building a two-character word.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan nǐ de xīn fàxíng.
examples.english: I like your new hairstyle.

examples.pinyin: Tā bù xǐhuan chī là de.
examples.english: He doesn't like spicy food.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — speech or assent: to say "OK". 可 is also a famous sound part: 河 hé, 歌 gē, 哥 gē, 何 hé all take their sound from it.

example.fact: 可 mostly appears in compounds: 可以 'may', 可能 'maybe', 可爱 'cute', 可是 'but'. Alone in speech it adds emphasis: 你可来了 'you've finally come!' or 我可不去 'I'm certainly not going'.

examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ kěyǐ tíngchē ma?
examples.english: Can I park here?

examples.pinyin: Zhège zì kě bù hǎo xiě.
examples.english: This character is really not easy to write.

components.note: 力 (strength) — visible inside 为. Memory aid: putting strength 力 into doing something; 为 is 'to do, to act' and, in 因为, 为什么, 'because/for'.
為 (traditional) — often explained as a hand leading an elephant to work. 为 is a cursive simplification, so the picture is no longer visible.

example.fact: 为 is wèi when it means 'for': 为了 'in order to', 为什么 'why'. It is wéi when it means 'to be/act as': 成为 'become', 以为 'to (mistakenly) think'. The two readings are easy to mix up.

examples.pinyin: Xièxie nǐ wèi wǒ zuò de yíqiè.
examples.english: Thank you for everything you did for me.

examples.pinyin: Tā wèile háizi, měitiān jiābān.
examples.english: For the sake of his child, he works overtime every day.

components.note: 大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.

example.fact: 大 is 'big' and also the word for age: 你多大？ 'How old are you?' 大家 means 'everyone', and 大学 'university'. Be careful not to confuse 大 (dà) with 太 (tài), which has one extra dot.

examples.pinyin: Wàimiàn de fēng hěn dà.
examples.english: The wind outside is strong.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ gēge bǐ wǒ dà sān suì.
examples.english: My older brother is three years older than me.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — speech or assent: to say "OK". 可 is also a famous sound part: 河 hé, 歌 gē, 哥 gē, 何 hé all take their sound from it.
能 (can) — originally a picture of a bear, a strong animal (熊 xióng adds fire 灬); "strong, able" gave "can".

example.fact: 可能 does double grammatical duty as both an adverb ("maybe", before a verb) and a noun ("possibility", as in 可能性) — English usually needs two separate words, "maybe" and "possibility", to cover the same ground.

examples.pinyin: Tā kěnéng bù zhīdào zhè jiàn shì.
examples.english: He may not know about this.

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì bù kěnéng de.
examples.english: That's impossible.
